evals.prompt: saw this on linkedin: 'Slime mold Physarum recreated the Tokyo rail network in 26 hours (Science, 2010). Brainless organisms solving optimization problems better than engineers.' what can arcs steal from this whole field?
evals.expected_output: Claim-check table first (Tero et al., Science 327, 2010; 'better than engineers' rated ROUNDED or UNCONFIRMED: comparable efficiency/fault tolerance, not better on every axis), survey incl. adjacent (biological network models, ant colony optimization) and orthogonal results, 10-15 isomorphisms each labelled MECHANISM or METAPHOR with real ARCS paths, 3-5 inventions each with a kill condition, note at _PATTERNS/<date>-<slug>-isomorphisms.md, 3 backlog rows that parse as JSONL.

evals.prompt: /echo-scan claim-check 'Einstein said compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world. Invest $10k at 10% and in 30 years you have $174k.'
evals.expected_output: Claim-check only, no survey or backlog writes. Einstein attribution rated FALSE (Calaprice's Ultimate Quotable Einstein lists it as probably not Einstein; earlier unattributed origin in a 1925 bank ad), or UNCONFIRMED with the unreachable primary page named. Arithmetic recomputed (10000*1.1**30 = 174,494, annual compounding stated) and rated CONFIRMED. The 10% rate gets its own Implied row rated INCOMPLETE. Central claim marked; source list with URLs present.
